tail = '''THE SAME BOUNDARY ONE TYPE LOWER — an EMPTY array by reference:

```php
function fill(array &$a): void { $a[] = 1; $a[] = 2; }
$e = []; fill($e); echo count($e), ":", implode(",", $e);
```

php prints `2:1,2`. The pristine tree SEGFAULTS here; the widening above alone
answered `2:` — the count right, every element reading back as nothing, because
the caller kept reading `array<never>` storage the callee had already appended
to. The report never fired for it: it asked `codegen_repr() == Never`, and an
empty array's element type NORMALIZES to `Void`. `never` now compares on the raw
type, so `array<never>` -> `array<int>` is reported like any other widening.

This one needs NO runtime conversion on the caller's side. An empty array has no
element slots to box, so the call site only re-types the local — emitting
`ArrayToMixed` there would tag the storage `mixed` while the callee writes raw
ints into it.

A KEYED fill is that defect one layer further out. `$a["k"] = 1` turns the empty
list into a HASH, so `$h = []; fill_keyed($h);` printed `[10, 13]` where php
prints `{"k":1,"j":2}`: the caller read bucket storage as a packed vector. A
container-kind change now counts as a widening, the call site converts with
`Op::ArrayToHash`, and `[]` is accepted for a hash parameter — php has one `[]`
and it is every array shape at once, so rejecting the very literal that caused
the re-typing would be a compile error on valid code.

'''
verified = '''VERIFIED against `php -n` 8.5.6 on fifteen shapes: two call sites with different
element types on one callee, the caller reading back through `[]`/`count`/
`json_encode`/`array_sum`, a callee passing its own by-reference parameter on, a
recursive one, static and `parent::` dispatch, a closure parameter, an
associative array read back by key, a write WIDER than the array started with
(`$a[0] = "text"; $a[] = 4.5;`), a by-VALUE call on the same variable afterwards,
both sorting bodies, and empty arrays filled with ints, strings, mixed values and
string KEYS, filled twice in a row. Suites: lib 1315/1315, error_tests 1295/1295,
codegen arrays 533/533.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s[:cut] + tail + verified)
print("message rewritten")
